recommendations.regimenLabel: Restore perfusion, stop nephrotoxins, treat the cause
steps: Assess volume status — fluid resuscitate if pre-renal/hypovolaemic; relieve obstruction (catheter/imaging) if post-renal.
Stop/avoid nephrotoxins (NSAIDs, ACEi/ARB, contrast, aminoglycosides); review drug doses.
Treat the cause (sepsis, obstruction, intrinsic disease); optimise perfusion and avoid both hypo- and hypervolaemia.
Monitor and treat complications — hyperkalaemia, acidosis, fluid overload, uraemia.
Urgent dialysis for refractory hyperkalaemia/acidosis/overload/uraemic complications; nephrology if intrinsic/unclear.

drugRefs.dose: 250–500 mL bolus, then titrated to volume status
drugRefs.freq: repeat to euvolaemia; reassess after each bolus
drugRefs.why: Restores renal perfusion in pre-renal/hypovolaemic AKI. Avoid over-filling once euvolaemic (risk of pulmonary oedema).

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Acute Kidney Injury
KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for Acute Kidney Injury

drugRefs.freq: repeat every 5–10 min if ECG changes persist
drugRefs.why: Stabilises the myocardium when hyperkalaemia causes ECG changes; does not lower serum K⁺.

drugRefs.dose: 10 units with 25 g glucose (e.g. 250 mL of 10%)
drugRefs.why: Drives K⁺ intracellularly; give with glucose to prevent hypoglycaemia.
Additional intracellular K⁺ shift; adjunct only, not a substitute for insulin–glucose.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Acute Kidney Injury
UK Renal Association / Renal Registry — Treatment of Acute Hyperkalaemia in Adults

confirm: Acute rise in creatinine and/or fall in urine output (KDIGO). Classify pre-renal / renal / post-renal.
